title: Defense Budget and Acquisition: Research & Analysis | CSIS
gist: CSIS topic landing page for Defense Budget and Acquisition with blurbs on recent work: drone swarms, federal AI spending ($4.1 billion since FY2019, 83 percent to DoD), allied burden sharing and air-and-missile-defense industrial base.

insights.claim: Federal agencies obligated $4.1 billion across 2,255 AI-related contracts since FY 2019, and 83 percent of those dollars went to the Defense Department.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: DoD dominates federal AI demand, so defense budgets drive AI vendor revenue.
insights.quote: Federal agencies obligated $4.1 billion across 2,255 AI-related contracts since FY 2019, and 83 percent of those dollars went to the Defense Department.
insights.locator: Understanding the U.S. Federal Government's AI Spending

insights.claim: CSIS argues cheap sensors and long-range fires make massing forces deadly, and that drone swarms paired with a clear operational concept can restore the offense, with use cases in Kaliningrad, the South China Sea and the Baltics.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Supports demand for swarming and counter-swarm capabilities.

insights.claim: Allies are spending more and building stronger defense industries, but the next era of burden sharing will depend on collective industrial capacity, not just defense budgets.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Co-production and munitions capacity among allies is the investable theme.

insights.claim: CSIS has work on rebuilding the air and missile defense industrial base for the salvo competition and on maritime electrification of US shipbuilding.
insights.speaker: CSIS
entities: air and missile defense industrial base
insights.so_what: Topics flag attention to interceptor production and electric shipbuilding.
